summary: the clock suite's case on x86-64, its one architecture, against the rule that counts one tick for each interrupt; the scenario times no line, so the judgment does not depend on when a line arrives

argv: ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 test-image && ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: one-per-interrupt
faults.summary: timer_tick_clock counting one tick for each interrupt once the reference keeps time, so that the host's stops lose the ticks that fell due, which the case finds as a drift of the guest's monotonic clock
